ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the two diagonals of rectangle $ABCD$ intersect at point $O$. If $AD=\sqrt{3}$ and $CD=1$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle ADB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given a rectangle ABCD,\\
it follows that $\angle BCD=90^\circ$, AD$\parallel$BC, and AD=BC.\\
Hence, $\angle ADB=\angle DBC$.\\
Thus, $BD=\sqrt{BC^{2}+CD^{2}}=\sqrt{(\sqrt{3})^{2}+1^{2}}=2$.\\
This means BD=2CD,\\
and so $\angle ADB=\angle DBC=30^\circ$.\\
Therefore, the answer is: $\boxed{30^\circ}$.
